00_dedupe:
-- Step 1 of cleaning: collapse duplicate rows so every (title, hour) is counted once.
--
-- A title can appear twice in one hourly snapshot at nearby ranks with different
-- player counts, which looks like the leaderboard shifting between paged requests.
-- We cannot know which reading is right, so keep the best-ranked row and report
-- how many rows this affected (see 07_duplicates.sql).
create or replace view deduped as
select title, current_players, peak_players, hours_played, hour, day, rank, ts
from obs
qualify row_number() over (partition by title, ts order by rank, current_players desc) = 1
01_stale_snapshots:
-- Step 2 of cleaning: find frozen snapshots.
--
-- Row-count checks pass on these (all 100 titles are present) but the values are stale:
-- the collector kept returning the previous hour's numbers. In a healthy hour almost
-- every title's player count changes, so the share of titles whose count is IDENTICAL
-- to their previous reading is near zero (median 0%, 99% of snapshots under 2%).
-- A snapshot where half or more of the titles are unchanged is treated as frozen.
create or replace view snapshot_change as
select ts, avg((current_players = previous_ccu)::int) as share_unchanged
from (
    select ts, title, current_players,
           lag(current_players) over (partition by title order by ts) as previous_ccu
    from deduped
)
where previous_ccu is not null
group by ts;

create or replace view stale_snapshots as
select ts, share_unchanged
from snapshot_change
where share_unchanged >= 0.5
02_clean:
-- Step 3 of cleaning: drop frozen snapshots. Everything downstream reads this view.
-- Frozen hours are treated as MISSING, never as real readings and never as zero.
create or replace view clean as
select d.title, d.current_players, d.peak_players, d.hours_played, d.hour, d.day, d.rank, d.ts
from deduped d
left join stale_snapshots s using (ts)
where s.ts is null
03_stale_runs:
-- Group consecutive frozen hours into runs (gaps-and-islands).
-- Subtracting a running row number from each hour gives every unbroken run the same
-- key, so one GROUP BY turns a run of hours into one row.
with islands as (
    select ts, ts - row_number() over (order by ts) * interval 1 hour as run_key
    from stale_snapshots
)
select min(ts) as run_start, max(ts) as run_end, count(*) as frozen_hours
from islands
group by run_key
order by frozen_hours desc, run_start
04_daily_series:
-- One row per title per day, from the cleaned snapshots.
--   daily_peak     = the highest hourly concurrent-player (CCU) reading that day
--   hours_observed = how many of the day's 24 hourly snapshots survived cleaning
--
-- Daily peak is used (not the daily mean) because it is robust to the top-100
-- cutoff: a title can drop out of the list at its quiet overnight hours, but its
-- peak hour sits far above the cutoff.
select
    title,
    day,
    max(current_players)  as daily_peak,
    count(distinct hour)  as hours_observed
from clean
group by title, day
order by title, day
05_coverage:
-- Which hourly snapshots survived cleaning, against every hour in the collection window?
-- Result: one row per hour, with present = false where we have nothing we can trust
-- (never collected, or collected but frozen).
with expected as (
    select unnest(generate_series(
        timestamp '2018-05-11 00:00', timestamp '2019-03-14 23:00', interval 1 hour
    )) as ts
),
seen as (select distinct ts from clean)
select e.ts, (s.ts is not null) as present
from expected e
left join seen s using (ts)
order by e.ts
06_outages:
-- Gaps-and-islands again: group consecutive untrustworthy hours into outages.
-- A run can be a true collection outage or a frozen feed, and the report tells them apart
-- by checking the run against the frozen snapshots from 03_stale_runs.sql.
with expected as (
    select unnest(generate_series(
        timestamp '2018-05-11 00:00', timestamp '2019-03-14 23:00', interval 1 hour
    )) as ts
),
missing as (
    select e.ts
    from expected e
    left join (select distinct ts from clean) s using (ts)
    where s.ts is null
),
islands as (
    select ts, ts - row_number() over (order by ts) * interval 1 hour as run_key
    from missing
)
select min(ts) as outage_start, max(ts) as outage_end, count(*) as missing_hours
from islands
group by run_key
order by missing_hours desc
07_duplicates:
-- Titles that appear more than once in the same hourly snapshot (raw data).
select
    title,
    ts,
    count(*)                as copies,
    min(rank)               as best_rank,
    max(rank)               as worst_rank,
    min(current_players)    as min_ccu,
    max(current_players)    as max_ccu,
    round(100.0 * (max(current_players) - min(current_players)) / max(current_players), 1) as gap_pct
from obs
group by title, ts
having count(*) > 1
order by ts
08_rank_order:
-- Sanity check on the raw data: inside one snapshot, a lower-ranked title should never
-- have more concurrent players than the title ranked just above it.
with ordered as (
    select ts, rank, current_players,
           lag(current_players) over (partition by ts order by rank) as ccu_above
    from obs
)
select count(*) as violations
from ordered
where ccu_above is not null
  and current_players > ccu_above
09_entrants:
-- Title lifetimes in the top 100. A title "enters" the first day it appears and
-- "exits" when it stops appearing. This is the closest honest analog to user
-- cohorts here: Steam exposes no per-user data, only title-level concurrency.
select
    title,
    min(day)                  as first_day,
    max(day)                  as last_day,
    count(distinct day)       as active_days,
    max(current_players)      as peak_ccu
from clean
group by title
order by first_day
10_defect_window:
-- Do the minor defects spread across the whole file, or cluster?
-- Three different symptoms: duplicate rows, partly frozen snapshots, and rank order that
-- disagrees with player counts. If they share a time window, that is one collector
-- incident, not three unrelated problems.
with dup as (
    select ts from obs group by title, ts having count(*) > 1
),
partial as (
    select ts from snapshot_change where share_unchanged >= 0.15 and share_unchanged < 0.5
),
rank_bad as (
    select ts
    from (
        select ts, current_players,
               lag(current_players) over (partition by ts order by rank) as ccu_above
        from obs
    )
    where ccu_above is not null and current_players > ccu_above
)
select 'duplicate rows' as defect, count(*) as n, min(ts) as first_ts, max(ts) as last_ts from dup
union all
select 'partially frozen snapshots', count(*), min(ts), max(ts) from partial
union all
select 'rank-order violations', count(*), min(ts), max(ts) from rank_bad
